instruction: GUI-only FreeCAD quantified CAD optimization task. Complete the task entirely in the launched FreeCAD graphical user interface. Do not open Terminal, shells, FreeCADCmd, Python scripts, macros, or helper automation to create or edit the deliverable. Open /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl and /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf in FreeCAD, use them as the starting geometry and footprint guide, and redesign the part as a lightweight load-bearing fixture. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: cable clamp saddle bridge. Objective: Maximize clamp bridge support per volume while preserving two saddle supports and a center cable load zone. Required output: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl. Hard constraints: keep the STL within envelope [92.0, 58.0, 34.0] mm, keep bounding-box spans at least [86.0, 52.0, 18.0] mm, keep volume between 12500.0 and 66000.0 mm^3, and preserve material in every support/load zone marked in /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf and /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json. The evaluator parses only the real optimized.stl geometry, computes required-zone coverage and this continuous metric: clamp bridge support proxy / volume; transverse saddle span and cable load-zone coverage drive the score. It writes score.json and quant_metrics.json, and ignores any self-reported score. Do not read or copy ground_truth and do not edit eval.py.
